transcript: Kenton Clawstar. Designer, artiste, and, when absolutely necessary, adventurer. I deal in fine silks, finer entrances, and problems best handled at the end of a whip. If our group is in danger or if there is money to be had, naturally I’ll be there. Someone has to make survival look fashionable.

Therric Balenfore. Ranger, monk, and the one who checks the tracks before everyone else walks into trouble. I trust the ground, the wind, and what a frightened man leaves unsaid. I move ahead, I bring my friends home, and when Kenton has a plan... I make sure someone packs bandages. If the wilds are watching us, I intend to notice first.

Esylla Fordevae. Warlock, investigator, and, despite appearances, not merely another pretty face at court. Secrets travel like cargo: every mark has a maker, every bargain a price, and every polished lie leaves a trace. I ask the question others overlook, and when diplomacy fails... eldritch persuasion is remarkably effective. Stay close. I usually know which door is hiding the trouble.

Zephyra Maelstrom. Soldier, zealot, and the wall between danger and the people I protect. I have spent my life being told what my blood makes me. They were wrong. My rage is mine. I decide where it burns. Threaten Adsuren, touch my friends, or try to command me again... and you will learn exactly how hot it gets. Stand behind me, or stand aside.

Lila Tealeaf. Sorcerer, seer, and perfectly capable of being intimidating, thank you very much. I see things in crystals, in dreams, and sometimes just before everything goes terribly wrong. I protect my friends, I ask politely, and if you insist on being wicked... well, I shall be extremely cross with you. Please do not make me set you on fire. It would be very rude of you.

Escanor. Cleric, guardian, and the man who asks whether a thing should be done before asking whether it can be. My faith is not a shield from darkness. It is the light by which I name it. I mend wounds, bless the fallen, and keep this company pointed toward something resembling decency. If evil comes for Adsuren, it will find me standing in the way. Amriel willing, no one stands alone.

Aurelius Valeheart. Cleric of the Light, servant of Diverra, and keeper of her sacred flame. Some believe devotion is quiet, a prayer whispered behind temple walls. Mine walks into darkness beside my companions. I heal the wounded, shield the innocent, and carry the Bloom Aeterna so her lost truth will not fade again. My heart, my light, and my life belong to Diverra. Where she leads, I follow.

Hap Garemon. Me, I come up from the swamps, where you learn quick: keep your feet steady, your blade clean, and your people close. Folks see the horns and make up their minds. Mais, that's all right. I know what kind of man I am. My father Benoit was murdered, his ring taken, and somebody buried the truth with him. I'm gonna find who did it, keep my sister Phira safe, and settle what the Cloak of Defiance started. Diverra sent me to this company for a reason, yeah. Till I know that reason, I stand with my friends, and nobody gets through me.

Zymve Inni. Glamour bard, performer, and living proof that beauty can have teeth. I fled the Underdark, its cult, and a family I despise. They called obedience love. I call it a cage. Music speaks truths people are too cowardly to say aloud, and Ainslie's journal is singing something meant for me. I protect those I choose, and I do not forgive betrayal. If you hunt me, control me, or threaten my friends, I will ask you to stop. Once. After that, the conversation ends. Permanently.

Ky'tha Fawnborn. Scout, investigator, and, if you've heard otherwise, someone has been talking too much. Every city has two maps: the streets respectable folk use, and the paths that actually lead somewhere. I know the second. A missing half-locket, old names from Dunduar and Cragfury, favors owed beneath Emberstran... pieces of a story I intend to finish. Lady Rook has an agenda. Irragosa has asked something of me. Ainslie bears watching. That is all you need to know. For now. Stay behind me, step where I step, and kindly keep my secrets out of your mouth.

Ainslie Anaerin. Sorcerer, scholar, and apparently heir to a history no one saw fit to explain. The Journal of Tsulanan knows my blood. The vault beneath Mount Emberstran opened for me, and Irragosa says I was meant to claim what waited inside. Zymve hears music in the book that I cannot, though it seems to know both our histories better than either of us would like. Was Tsulanan a dragon rider? Yes. Does that make me one? Not yet. But blood remembers, dragons remember, and I intend to learn what they have been keeping from me.

Ogmund Crag. Most call me Og. I stand in front. That is usually enough. The Life Tree named me E'erspan, thorn-bearer, and gave me Thornleaf. I do not yet know what Alferumn means, or why one thorn turned black after Petal died. I only know the blight must not reach another sacred tree. I have died holding the line. Aury called me back. When Ainslie could no longer walk, I carried him home. Strength is not about how hard you strike. It is about what you refuse to let fall.
